text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Heavy flash floods cause havoc across Kenya.
- An attempt to raid a National Bank of Kenya branch in Nairobi by three armed gangsters foiled by police.
- At least 300 heavily armed cattle rustlers from the Pokot community in west of the Rift Valley attack their neighbours in Marakwet.
- Leaders of opposition FORD-Asili party say they will not endorse their chairman Kenneth Matiba as the party's presidential candidate in general elections sometime this year.
- Ruling KANU party grassroot elections begin in central province, which is dominated by the opposition parties.
- The government suspends the transportation of food between Mandera and Wajir districts in northeastern Kenya following an outbreak of cholera.
- A Nairobi court sets free four people charged with robbing the Standard Chartered Bank of 96 million shillings ($1.8 million) in February.
- The government signs a 40-million-shilling agreement with Britain to support micro-enterprises.
- Kenya Ports Authority Executive Chairman Robert Breineissen announces he will retire next week.
- A silent revolution is taking place against President Daniel arap Moi among members of his Kalenjin community and other minority groups that are disillusioned with his leadership.
